title: Habitats & Adaptation
source: Science G3 B1 Study sheet pp.10-12, Worksheet Q5-Q6

scenes.t: A habitat is the place where an animal lives. It is the animal's home that gives it food, water and shelter.
In the cold Arctic habitat live polar bears, penguins, polar foxes and seals. They have thick fur or feathers to stay warm.
In the hot, dry desert live camels, snakes, scorpions and tortoises. They can live a long time without water.
Seas and rivers are aquatic habitats. Fish, octopuses, sharks and whales live there. Fish breathe with gills and swim with fins.
A grassland gets enough rain for grass, but not for trees. Zebras, lions, cheetahs and ostriches live there.
A forest has lots of tall trees because it gets plenty of rain. Monkeys, parrots, tigers and deer live there.
Adaptation means the features that help a living thing survive in its habitat. The camel has padded feet so it does not sink in the sand, and a hump to store food.
The penguin has thick feathers and a fatty layer called blubber to keep warm, and webbed feet for swimming. A fish cannot live on land: it has no legs and its gills cannot breathe air.

items.a: The place where an animal lives and finds food, water and shelter.
Features that help a living thing survive in its habitat.
Very cold. Polar bear, penguin, seal.
Hot, sandy, few plants. Camel, scorpion.
Lots of grass, few trees. Zebra, lion.
Many tall trees. Monkey, parrot, tiger.
A thick fatty layer that keeps penguins and seals warm.

activities.title: The Blubber Glove
activities.goal: Feel how blubber keeps a penguin warm.
activities.safe: Ask an adult to help you. Take your hand out if it gets too cold.

predict.q: Which hand will feel colder in the ice water?
o: The hand in the fat (blubber) bag

steps.t: Put the fat inside one zip bag.
Put your hand in the second bag, then push it into the fat bag and squish the fat all around it. This is your blubber glove!
Put your other hand, with no glove, in the ice water for a few seconds.
Now put the blubber glove hand in the ice water. Compare how both hands feel.

activities.result: The bare hand gets cold very fast, but the blubber glove hand stays warm for much longer!
activities.why: Fat slows down the cold. Penguins, seals and whales have blubber, an adaptation for the cold Arctic habitat.
